Brainstem involvement as onset of stiff limb syndrome: A case report
F. Ceriani, N. Massetto, C. Rosci, M. Pietrogrande (Milan, Italy)
Background: The stiff limb syndrome seems distinct from the stiff man
syndrome or progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity. Patients have
rigidity, painful spasm with abnormal postures of the distal limb and may
follow sphincter (50%) or brainstem (40% of cases) involvement with
relapsing and remitting course; most patients have no evidence of autoim-
mune disease.
Case Report: We describe the case of a 66-year-old woman who 5
years ago, after recovery from peripheral right facial nerve palsy,
developed subacute onset of dysarthria, rhinolalia and severe dysphagia
with lips, tongue and velum palatinum paresis. Brain MRI, CFS and
EMG repetitive stimulation were normal, Ach-R antibodies were ab-
sent. Three months later, while improving, she began to complain
painful lower limbs spasms with dif ﬁculty in walking and frequent falls.
The EMG study revealed the presence of continuous motor unit activity
in lower limbs muscles at rest and diazepam therapy was successfully
prescribed. Eight month later, in combination with a worsening of the
legs rigidity, she began to complain about diplopia with signs of
bilateral ophthalmoplegia. A series of examinations (thyroid function-
ality, autoantibodies, neoplastic markers, abdomen and pelvic echogra-
phy, chest CT, mammography) did not show signi ﬁcant results in
favour of a paraneoplastic or autoimmune disorder; moreover Borrelia
B. Ig and serum anti-GAD antibodies were absent, angiotensin conver-
tase was normal. In few days the prednisone administration led to a
prompt improvement of both ocular and legs symptoms. After 18
months the symptoms reappeared following the reduction of pred-
nisone, from 50 to 25 mg/day, and were initiated cycles of immuno-
globuline every 3 months with good results. However 14 months later,
the patient a morning didn ’ts u c c e e di no p e n i n gt h ee y e l i d sf o rc o m p l e t e
bilateral ptosis and despite the steroid administration, the symptoms
have disappeared only after 4 months. At present the patient has been
being asymptomatic for 8 months with the combined therapy of pred-
nisone (10 mg/day) and immunoglobuline.
Conclusions: The interest of our case of stiff limb case lies in the onset
with brainstem involvement, usually delayed by several years, before any
evidence of leg spasm; besides relapses in the cranial district were com-
bined to the worsening of the rigidity that however has remained exclu-
sively located for 5 years to the lower limbs.
